# Review of iliad-124 (Iliad 19.154–237)

Two passes. Pass 1: notes against the Greek and the packet (labels, positions, cross-references), then Greek → `l` → `i`, house table, remembered English, quotation marks against the neighbouring part (iliad-123 ends on the closing ” of Achilles’ speech; this part opens with the formula, so no speech runs over). Pass 2: re-read every edited unit against the Greek and the table, checked `l`/`t` line counts, quote balance between `l` and `i`, `mark`/`p` placement, and that `t` is byte-identical to before. `t` was not touched. No scansion flags in the packet, so no metrical sentence was added.

Severity: major = breaks a binding table row or states something false; moderate = wrong or misleading in sense/force or a note claim; minor = polish.

## Changes (line · field · severity · wrong · done)

- 19.154 · n · moderate · "προσέφη is an aorist without augment" is false: προσέφη is the past of προσφημί and carries its own ε-. · Now "the past tense of προσφημί, ‘addressed’".
- 19.155 · i, n · moderate · ὄτρυνε rendered "drive … on"; the table has ὀτρύνω "urge on" (4.73, 4.268). · "urge … on" in `i`; note follows.
- 19.160 · i · minor · "eat and drink" for πάσασθαι … σίτου καὶ οἴνοιο loses "wine"/the genitive object. · "take food and wine".
- 19.161 · l, i, n · major · Drafter's departure ("might and prowess") contradicts the table row for this exact clause (9.706): "for that is strength and might"; the drafter's claim that the table gives ἀλκή "might" and μένος "might" missed that row, and "prowess" is among the words the table turns down for ἀλκή (5.299). · `l` and `i` set to the table's English; note rewritten (says μένος is "might" elsewhere but "strength" in this pair, as at 9.706); note also now says the unit begins mid-line 161 (was missing). The `μένος καὶ ἀλκή` row was removed from `new-renderings.md`.
- 19.162 · i, n · moderate · `i` "if he has been given no food" adds a condition and drops γάρ; note said ἄντα means "in the front line", contradicting `l`/`i` "face to face". · `i` now "For no man, without food, will be able to fight face to face …"; the front-line gloss removed.
- 19.177 · n · minor · Asserted flatly that ἄναξ is a vocative to Achilles; the edition prints no commas and the construction can be read otherwise. · Hedged ("most naturally a vocative"). `l`/`i` unchanged.
- 19.178 · i · minor · "must have" turns the 3rd-person imperative ἔστω into a plain obligation. · "let the heart in your mind be gracious".
- 19.182–183 · i, n · moderate · (Drafter flag 183 τις.) `i` "when he was the first to be angry" is past and particular, but ὅτε … χαλεπήνῃ is a general subjunctive; "nothing to be resented" left the table's "a thing to resent" (3.410). The note's "the offender is the king himself" is not in the Greek. · `i` now "not at all a thing to resent … whenever someone has been the first to be harsh"; note says the Greek leaves τις unnamed and that in this setting the one who began the quarrel is the king.
- 19.184 · n · minor · "προσέειπεν is an unaugmented aorist" is false (the ε- is the augment, doubled). · "the epic aorist of προσεῖπον". `l`/`i` identical to the published iliad-053 unit.
- 19.185 · i · minor · "hearing" for aorist ἀκούσας. · "having heard your speech".
- 19.188 · l, n · moderate · ἐπειγόμενός περ Ἄρηος has a table row (19.142): "pressing on to Ares" / "eager … for battle". `l` had "eager for Ares". · `l` "though pressing on to Ares"; note says `l` keeps the god's name.
- 19.193 · l · minor · Παναχαιῶν: table `l` is "of the Achaeans all together". · "the best men of the Achaeans all together".
- 19.196 · i · minor · "to be slaughtered to Zeus" makes the active infinitive passive and uses "to" for the god. · "to slaughter for Zeus and the Sun".
- 19.199 · n · moderate · Note called ὀφέλλετε a form of ὀφέλλω "ought"; the table keeps ὀφέλλω "increase" apart from ὀφείλω "ought". Also the οὐ τόσον sentence was ambiguous. · Now "doubled-λ form of ὀφείλω … (not ὀφέλλω ‘increase’)"; οὐ τόσον clarified.
- 19.203 · i, n · moderate · (Drafter flag 205 ὀτρύνετον.) "press for food" shifts the sense (and the table has "urge"); the mood was not stated. The 2nd-dual ending is the same in indicative and imperative; the indicative is right ("you two urge [us] to food"). · `i` "you two urge us on to food"; note says present dual, same ending as the imperative, sense a statement, object unspoken.
- 19.205 · l, n · major (l), moderate (n) · (Drafter flag 208 τεισαίμεθα.) `l` broke the line division: line 1 held the words of Greek line 2, and "to fight" lost its "to". The note gave no mood: τεισαίμεθα is an aorist optative (a subjunctive would be τεισώμεθα), unusual after ἐπήν and drawn to the optative ἀνώγοιμι. Also "dative of time" was imprecise and "outrage done to the Achaeans by Hector’s killing" over-specified. · `l` re-divided to four lines matching `t`; note now names the optative and its reason, "ἅμα with a dative participle", and "the outrage of the dead".
- 19.209 · i · moderate · (Drafter flag 212.) `i` "with any welcome" is not English; "turned about in the forecourt" disagreed with `l` "up along the forecourt" and with the note's "along". · `i` "could go down my throat gladly … turned about along the forecourt". The note already says the line does not say which way he is turned; ἀνά with the accusative is not "in".
- 19.212 · n · minor · "the men of Achilles’ hut" is more than ἑταῖροι says. · "the rest of Achilles’ companions".
- 19.221 · i, l · moderate · `i` "battle-din" where the table's `i` is "the din of battle"; `l` ended "Zeus, who of men the steward of war has been made", not the published 19.224 order. · `i` "a fullness of the din of battle … in which"; `l` "who of men has been made the steward of war".
- 19.226 · l, i, n · major · ἐπήτριμοι: table (18.211) gives "close-set" / "close together" and turns down "thick". · `l` "close-set", `i` "close together", note follows.
- 19.227 · n · minor · Unit begins mid-line 227 but the note did not say so (every other mid-line start does). · Sentence added.
- 19.230 · n · moderate · (Drafter flag 230 περὶ στυγεροῖο.) Note said περί "is best read as ‘out of’", overclaiming. · Now: περί follows its noun; its force with λίπωνται is not certain; "left over from the war" likeliest, against "left in the fighting around it". `l`/`i` unchanged.
- 19.233 · l, i, n · major · ἰσχαναάσθω: the table keeps ἰσχανάω "hold back" and turns down "hung back" (12.38). · `l` "hold himself back", `i` "hold back", note follows.
- 19.236–237 · n · minor · (Drafter flag 237 ἐγείρομεν.) Hortative reading kept (see refused). Note now says the same form is a plain indicative at 4.352 and why it is hortative here. `l`/`i` unchanged.
- 19.167–170 · l, i, n · major · ἐρωῆσαι πολέμοιο has a table row (13.776): "hold back from war", turning down "draw back from". · `l` "have held back from war", `i` "has held back from the war", note follows.

## Findings considered and refused

- 19.237 ἐγείρομεν, published 4.352 indicative ("are rousing"). Refused to match it: the whole-unit rule does not apply (the unit begins at ἀλλ’ ἀθρόοι), and ἀλλά with ὁρμηθέντες makes the call "let us rouse". Table English for ὀξὺν Ἄρηα kept.
- 19.205 ὀτρύνετον as imperative. Refused: the sense is a statement ("you two urge"), not a command to the pair.
- 19.212 ἀνὰ πρόθυρον τετραμμένος: no direction supplied ("toward the door" would be a guess); "turned about" kept in both layers and the note's admission stands.
- 19.192 `i` "this charge and this command" for τόδε … ἐπιτέλλομαι ἠδὲ κελεύω: a noun for two verbs, but the force is kept; refused.
- 19.186 `l` aorists rendered as perfects ("you have gone through"); idiomatic in both layers; refused.
- 19.209 ἑταίρου τεθνηῶτος "genitive absolute": checked, correct (the following relative ὅς is nominative).
- 19.171 ὅπλεσθαι "infinitive of ὁπλίζομαι": the formation is debated, the note only glosses the meaning; refused.
- 19.220 τοι "dative or particle": the note already says either fits.
- 19.205 `i` omits ἦ τε "truly": particle only; refused.
- Scansion: packet flags none; nothing to scan or annotate.
- Quotation marks: “ on 155, 185, 199, 216; ” on 183 (unit at 182), 197 (196), 214 (213), 237 (236); `mark` on exactly those four first units; `p` on 154, 184, 198, 215. All correct; no change.
- Repeated lines: 154/215, 184, 198, 199 (Ἀτρεΐδη … Ἀγάμεμνον), 216, 176 `l`/`i` agree with the published English.

## Counts

Major 5 (19.161, 19.205 `l`, 19.226, 19.233, 19.167), moderate 11, minor 10. Pass 2 found no further errors in the edited text.
